frontier.hypothesis: The last unmeasured leg of cse.c:849-857 is clause (1): if block 0's cse EBB ended AFTER i's last reference, i would fail the `uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[new]] > cse_basic_block_end` test, a0 would stay qty_first_reg, and the i-first chassis would keep `sll $v1,$s2,4` -- a byte match, since s50 already proved i-first reproduces the target's whole block-0 schedule and allocation.
frontier.mechanism: cse's EBB for block 0 is `;; Processing block from 2 to 37` (dumps_B/text1a_c.cse); it stops at loop 1's top label, which has two predecessors. i's last reference is in loop 2, far beyond 37. The disjunct's other half (`uid_cuid[regno_first_uid[new]] < cse_basic_block_start`) is already false in block 0 because the EBB starts at the function head, so clause (1) rests entirely on where the EBB ends. Crucially the preheader EBB (`from 71 to 110`) satisfies clause (1) via the OTHER disjunct, so an EBB-boundary attack changes block 0 WITHOUT disturbing the preheader -- unlike every clause-(2) attack, which is global and flips both shifts together.
frontier.next_probe: Read cse_end_of_basic_block in tools/gcc-2.7.2/cse.c and enumerate exactly what makes it stop at insn 37 (label uses / follow_jumps / skip_blocks), then enumerate ONLY source spellings that move that boundary: loop 1 written so its top label falls later or is single-predecessor, an if/comma/statement grouping that extends the first EBB past loop 1, or a loop-1 shape whose backedge target is not a shared label. Confirm each candidate by grepping the `;; Processing block from` lines in the .cse dump BEFORE spending a sandbox run, and reject anything at build_insns != 83.

frontier.hypothesis: The two complementary score-2 forms can still be merged: some third spelling gets candidate.c's correct `sll` operands AND the s50 chassis's correct block-0 schedule.
frontier.mechanism: After s51 the merge needs exactly one thing: an RTL insn stream in which the shift's LUID exceeds `i = a0`'s (scheduler side, now closed at both passes -- so this must come from the SOURCE order) while cse still leaves the shift's operand rtx as a0. Every clause-(2) route is now measured dead: shorten i's last use (allocation collapse, 80 insns), lift a0's reg_n_refs (fixes the allocation only, +1 insn), lengthen a0's last use (jump.c:577, this session). Only clause (1) is left, which is frontier item 1.
frontier.next_probe: Treat frontier item 1 as the merge probe -- it is the same experiment. If an EBB-boundary spelling exists at build_insns == 83, dump .cse and check that block 0's ashift still reads reg 72 while the loop-2 preheader's still reads the i pseudo; that combination is the byte match.

frontier.hypothesis: A construct that creates block 0's shift insn AFTER cse has run (so canon_reg never sees its operand) would satisfy both sides simultaneously without touching either cse clause.
frontier.mechanism: cse only rewrites operands of insns it walks. An insn materialised later -- a loop.c-emitted preheader initial value for an induction variable, or a combine-formed shift whose operands were fixed pre-cse -- would carry a0 into sched2 with a high LUID. Note cse RUNS TWICE (a .cse2 dump exists), so any such insn must also survive cse2's canonicalisation, which re-establishes the same quantity from the same `i = a0` copy.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80045294/s51/dumps_cand/text1a_c.loop and .combine for block 0 and list which of its insns are CREATED after cse at all; then check the same insns in .cse2. If none of block 0's insns can be created post-cse, and cse2 re-canonicalises anything that could be, that closes the merge by construction and the informed floor is 2.
